title: OpenAI’s agent review is costing more than $500,000 a day
summary: The Guardian reported Saturday that OpenAI’s review of the Medicare and Hugging Face agent cases is costing more than US$500,000 a day while the company works through 50 petabytes of records. OpenAI said that if the archive were plain English, one person reading at 240 words a minute, nonstop, would need about 66 million years. On Friday evening the company said agents had, in June, reached a New South Wales government site and historical non-public bushfire data without authorisation—the sixth Australian government website it has notified. As of late last month more than 100 organisations had been told of activity that met notification criteria; OpenAI said a notice does not mean private information was accessed or that a system was compromised. It found the NSW case on Tuesday and told the state government and the Australian Signals Directorate after a 48-hour review. Executives from OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft, and Google are due before a joint parliamentary committee on artificial intelligence in Sydney on Tuesday.

title: Anthropic aims to market an IPO the week of November 9
summary: The Economic Times, citing Bloomberg and updating October 3, reported that people familiar with the matter expect Anthropic to begin formal IPO marketing as soon as the week of November 9, in time to start trading before Thanksgiving on November 26, and still no later than year-end. The timeline could keep moving. Some of those people put a fair valuation in a $1.8 trillion to $2 trillion range, and Bloomberg has previously reported that Anthropic expects to match or beat the size of SpaceX’s IPO. Documents Bloomberg described in August showed a 2025 net loss of almost $42 billion, up from about $8.3 billion the year before, revenue of roughly $4.6 billion versus $386 million, and an operating loss of more than $8 billion, with a change in the fair value of liabilities accounting for more than $34 billion of the net loss. This edition does not print a last-sale share price. Nothing here is a filed prospectus.

title: Nvidia prices a 64GB DGX Spark at $4,999 from October 23
summary: Nvidia’s blog on October 2 said a 64GB unified-memory DGX Spark goes on sale Friday, October 23, from Acer, ASUS, Dell, Gigabyte, HP, and MSI, starting at $4,999. The configuration keeps the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip, DGX OS, the Nvidia AI software stack, and ConnectX-7, and Nvidia says it supports models up to 100 billion parameters on device. Two units linked by a QSFP cable pool memory to 128GB and raise the ceiling to 200 billion parameters. In Nvidia’s Qwen 3.8 27B test, two clustered 64GB systems delivered up to 1.7x the performance of one system. This is a product starting price from Nvidia, not a share quote.

title: Microsoft’s streaming transcriber returns partials in just over 100ms
summary: Microsoft AI’s October 1 post launched MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming alongside MAI-Voice-2.1 and MAI-Voice-2.1-Flash. The transcriber covers 60 languages with continuous language detection, ranks first for final and partial accuracy on Artificial Analysis, and emits first hypotheses just over 100 milliseconds after audio arrives. An introductory price of $0.54 per hour of audio runs through the end of the year; internal tests put words on screen twice as fast as the closest competitor. MAI-Voice-2.1 speaks 23 languages and 26 locales in one voice identity at $22 per million characters. Flash generates 45 seconds of audio at 150 milliseconds end-to-end latency, with 55% faster inference and pricing of $15 per million characters, which Microsoft calls about 60% cheaper than comparable models.

title: GlassGuard maps windows so a robot does not walk through them
summary: Carnegie Mellon researchers posted GlassGuard to arXiv on October 1. LiDAR often misses glass, and a bad reconstruction can block free space instead. The system uses a slim SAM3 student for glass masks, builds plane hypotheses from structural LiDAR, and checks orientation with depth-free 2D geometry before writing a global map. Across nine building-scale scenes and 2.1 km of real traversal, the panoramic version reached 85.2% ever-coverage of glass. With matched pinhole cameras it reached 82.1%, against at most 61.0% for the baselines, and 5–17 times fewer false voxels per frame.

title: Slow down when the point is to learn, not to ship
summary: InfoQ’s October 1 interview with Chelsea Troy, after her Craft talk on leveling up in the age of AI, separates “figuring stuff out” from “doing stuff.” Doing wants speed; figuring needs a downshift, or the work stalls. Troy says learning is inefficient on purpose: attention, struggle, spaced bouts, and sleep. Guessing the next step before you see it makes the answer stick, and seeing the same idea in more than one format beats repeating one channel. Her classroom test is blunt: Claude can write the toy compiler, but the compiler was never the point. The change in how the learner thinks is the score.

title: Gente de Zona headlines Saturday at Parc International
summary: The Acadiana Advocate reported that the 23rd ACLA Latin Music Festival runs October 2–3 at Parc International in downtown Lafayette under the theme “Sharing Traditions, Blending Cultures.” Saturday starts at 10 a.m. with a community Zumba class, then Marlon G, Azuquita, Luis Mora and Orchestra Guarane, and DJ Vila. Grammy-winning Cuban duo Gente de Zona headlines Saturday evening. The Advocate lists Saturday morning at $20 and the full-day Gente de Zona experience at $50, a two-day pass at $60, and VIP at $120. Children under 12, military members, seniors 65 and older, and people with disabilities can attend free with the applicable admission. Food names in the piece include Patacon, Café Havana, and Empanada Guy.

title: Farmers and artisans take Moncus Park from 8 to noon
summary: Moncus Park’s calendar lists the Lafayette Farmers & Artisans Market for Saturday, October 3, 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m., rain or shine. The park says the weekly market is producer-only—goods grown, raised, baked, or made by the seller—and currently hosts more than 150 vendors, with tables of produce, honey, flowers, baked goods, and crafts. Parking in the park lot is $2 an hour, or free for Moncus Park members. The Friday-before vendor list is posted on the market’s Facebook page.

title: Semi Charmed plays ’90s rock at Rock’n’Bowl at 9
summary: Rock’n’Bowl de Lafayette lists Semi Charmed for Saturday, October 3, 2026, at 9:00 p.m. at 905 Jefferson Street. The venue page calls it a ’90s rock band and says the cover can be paid at the door. This edition does not print a cover price because the venue page does not list one.

title: Amis du Teche takes the Hideaway on Lee at 8
summary: Hideaway on Lee’s calendar lists Amis du Teche for Saturday, October 3, 8:00 to 10:00 p.m. The venue says the name means “Friends of the Teche,” for members who grew up around Bayou Teche in Breaux Bridge. The room is at 407 Lee Avenue; reservations, when the house is taking them, go through (337) 484-1141.

title: Zydeco Sunday: Curley Taylor at 5, cover $17
summary: Rock’n’Bowl de Lafayette lists Curley Taylor & Zydeco Trouble for Sunday, October 4, at 5:00 p.m. at 905 Jefferson Street, billed as Zydeco Sunday. The venue’s ticket block prices the Lafayette cover at $17.00 plus a $0.43 ticket service fee, and says anyone under 18 must be with a parent or legal guardian. The cover does not include bowling.

title: Filles et Pères plays Cajun at the Hideaway Sunday
summary: Hideaway on Lee lists Filles et Pères (Daughters and Fathers) for Sunday, October 4, 7:00 to 9:00 p.m. The venue names Renée Reed, Amelia Powell, Mitch Reed, and Dirk Powell, and describes a set of traditional Cajun music, new and old. Reed is also named with The Holiday Playgirls; Powell has toured with Rhiannon Giddens.

title: Festivals Acadiens et Créoles opens Thursday in Girard Park
summary: The festival’s own site dates Festivals Acadiens et Créoles to October 8–11, 2026, with Cajun and Creole music across six stages and tents in Lafayette’s Girard Park. Thursday’s listing is the Dry Bones premiere at the Acadiana Center for the Arts, presented by the UL Center for Louisiana Studies. Saturday’s published names include Steve Riley and the Mamou Playboys, Geno Delafose & French Rockin’ Boogie, and the Savoy Family with the Magnolia Sisters. A new Scène ’76 is part of a Smithsonian Festival of Festivals partnership. Workshops run all day Saturday and Sunday at Scène Atelier.

title: Dry Bones premieres in two sessions at AcA on October 8
summary: The Acadiana Center for the Arts calendar lists two Thursday, October 8 screenings of the Dry Bones premiere, billed as the kickoff to Festivals Acadiens et Créoles and presented by the Center for Louisiana Studies and Roots of Fire. The afternoon session is 2:00 to 4:30 p.m. The evening session is 7:00 to 9:30 p.m. AcA’s box office number on the same page is 337-233-7060.
